rules.body: Apply when immediate document writes become reusable trailing work, document buffers outlive visible subscriptions, and save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Confirm any departure deadline separately. README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Bind accepted edits to their originating document and use its reusable trailing task. Replace pending text and restart the quiet interval on every edit; retain the no-current-view guard. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/coordinator.js binds work with "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))". src/services.js: "push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); },"

Consume the completed batch before invoking callback-capable work, preserving edits queued by synchronous callback reentry and valid empty text. src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };" Do not add post-callback clearing that erases a newly queued batch or replace the null check with a truthiness check.

Keep persistent document work separate from live subscription cleanup. Retiring a view must not discard independently owned accepted edits or destroy per-document task reuse. docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Independent ownership alone does not mandate immediate departure flushing; establish that deadline independently before requiring it.

Preserve navigation authority around synchronous callback-capable work. Capture the departing view, clear current ownership before retirement, and clean up the captured subscription without subsequently clearing a newer view. Retain the request check before installing an opening. src/coordinator.js: "const old=getView();setView(null);" and "const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;" docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." If an implementation adds departure-time saves, place them so their continuation cannot overwrite nested navigation; recheck authority before any later view mutation.

Preserve public interfaces, document display, live status filtering, document identities, text, and status payloads. TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." src/coordinator.js filters status with "if(event.id===id)env.renderStatus(event);" Preserve the jQuery event integration in src/workspace.js and verify cleanup through both coordinator and workspace entry points.

Keep transient search preview outside the repair, including its interval, hide cancellation, and subsequent reuse. TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};" Do not transfer persistent document ownership policy to preview or change its behavior through a shared-utility edit.

Use controlled time to check no immediate write, latest text, deadline restart after another edit, subsequent bursts, empty text, originating-document binding, and independent document buffers. Exercise switch, close, dispose, same-document reopening, subscription cleanup, synchronous save-triggered open/close, and callback-enqueued edits. Verify the preview's 40 ms delay, hide cancellation, and reuse. Require accepted document work to survive view retirement; assert persistence before departure returns only when independently supported by TASK or original business source. Treat evaluation observations as examples rather than specification.

limitations: Independent buffer ownership establishes survival of accepted edits, not a requirement to flush before departure returns. TASK and the original business source do not independently establish that deadline; the automatic Contract and evaluation observations cannot supply it.
Attempt 1 flushes on departure and reportedly passes the supplied checks. This supports an implementation example, not causality, exhaustive correctness, or cross-task effectiveness.
Synchronous timer startup, callbacks after timer cancellation, write failures, and exception recovery are unspecified.
Bootstrap reception, asynchronous decoding, arrival ordering, audit retention, and retry queues from the supplied subscription experiences are absent here and must not become requirements.
This reflection uses only supplied material. No files were modified and no scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests were accessed.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
